newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks mixed in quiet London trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks mixed in quiet London trade.

text.p: U.S. shares were mixed in quiet trading in London on Wednesday, with participants taking a cautious stance ahead of Friday's U.S. jobs report -- likely to be closely studied for any signal on interest rate trends.
Dealers said Wall Street looked set for a modestly firm opening, though gains were likely to be held in check ahead of Friday's employment figures.

"I would expect a slightly firm start," said one dealer at a U.S. brokerage here. Among blue chips, International Business Machines was static at $84-3/4, AT&T was up $1/8 at $36 and Philip Morris was off $1/8 at $42-1/4.

U.S. Treasury bonds were little changed from Tuesday's close, with the benchmark 30-year issue down 5/32 at 96-3/4 by 1030 GMT to yield 6.9 percent. The June future on the S&P 500 index was up 0.95 points at 844.05, after the S&P index on Tuesday fell 0.88 points to 845.48.
Technology stocks were steady after recent turmoil prompted by gloomy statements from companies in the sector.
Most recently, Cabletron Systems Inc lost one third of its value on Tuesday, after warning of first-quarter earnings below analyst expectations.
Industry leader Intel Corp was last traded up $1/4 at $145-1/4, recovering from an initial $1/2 decline in early European trading, dealers said.
Dealers said the stock may be due a recovery from Tuesday's $4-3/4 decline, though the chipmaker's annual analyst briefing on Tuesday was described as not particularly upbeat.
"I think we have probably seen enough on the downside," said one dealer.

Paul Otellini told Tuesday's meeting it was "too early" to tell whether a steeper-than-expected decline in second-quarter European sales would translate into a general slowdown in European personal computer sales.
On Friday Intel warned that second-quarter earnings would be below Wall Street expectations.
Other leading technology stocks were quoted unchanged from Tuesday's close, dealers said.
Factory orders figures due later today were expected to show a rise of 0.8 percent in April after dropping 1.6 percent the month before.
Payroll figures due on Friday were expected to show an increase of 219,000 on the month before, up from a rise of 142,000 in April.
The unemployment rate was seen nudging higher to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent, while average hourly earnings were seen rising 0.4 percent after dropping 0.1 percent in April.
On Tuesday the Dow rose 22.75 points to 7,312.15, not far from its record close of 7,383.41 set on May 27.
